The DOCX path via pandoc is working. Now let me test the pdftotext fast path. Need to create a text-based PDF. Can use pandoc in the container to generate a PDF, but... pandoc needs a PDF engine (pdflatex, wkhtmltopdf, etc.), which might not be installed. Let me check. As an alternative, I could check if Python's reportlab is available, or use some other method.

Actually, I might be able to create a minimal text-based PDF manually (raw PDF syntax containing a text object). If I write it by hand, a simple 1-page PDF with Helvetica text should be processable by pdftotext. Let me create a minimal PDF.

Minimal PDF:

```
%PDF-1.4
1 0 obj
<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>
endobj
2 0 obj
<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>
endobj
3 0 obj
<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents 4 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R >> >> >>
endobj
4 0 obj
<< /Length 60 >>
stream
BT /F1 24 Tf 72 720 Td (Hello open_taki pdftotext fast path test) Tj ET
endstream
endobj
5 0 obj
<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>
endobj
xref
...
trailer
<< /Size 6 /Root 1 0 R >>
startxref
...
%%EOF
```

The xref offsets have to be correct. I could write a small Python script to generate a valid PDF with correct offsets, or use printf and compute the offsets. Python is probably available on the host. Let me check and write a script.

Actually, an even simpler approach: python3 is probably installed. Let me write a small generator.

Also, I need to double-check the fallback settings: min_chars: 200, min_chars_per_page: 50. The text needs to be at least 200 characters total, and at least 50 characters per page. Let me make the PDF text long enough — around 250 characters.

Let me test this.

action.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
text = "Hello open_taki. This is a text-based PDF generated for validation of the pdftotext fast path. It needs to exceed two hundred characters in total so that the fallback min_chars threshold of two hundred is satisfied and no LLM call is attempted. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
print(len(text))
# Build minimal single-page PDF
objs = []
objs.append(b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>")
objs.append(b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>")
objs.append(b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents 4 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R >> >> >>")
stream = ("BT /F1 11 Tf 72 720 Td (" + text + ") Tj ET").encode()
objs.append(b"<< /Length " + str(len(stream)).encode() + b" >>\nstream\n" + stream + b"\nendstream")
objs.append(b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>")
out = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.4\n")
offsets = []
for i, o in enumerate(objs, 1):
    offsets.append(len(out))
    out += str(i).encode() + b" 0 obj\n" + o + b"\nendobj\n"
xref_pos = len(out)
out += b"xref\n0 " + str(len(objs)+1).encode() + b"\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
for off in offsets:
    out += ("%010d 00000 n \n" % off).encode()
out += b"trailer\n<< /Size " + str(len(objs)+1).encode() + b" /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n" + str(xref_pos).encode() + b"\n%%EOF\n"
open("/tmp/test.pdf","wb").write(bytes(out))
print("pdf written")
EOF
curl -sS -X PUT --data-binary @/tmp/test.pdf -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" http://localhost:9998/rmeta/text -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\n"
